concerns: Run 1 wins 4 of 5 folds against run 3 (fold 4 goes to run 3, 0.8123 vs 0.8014) and all 5 against run 2, so it is the most consistent config, though only 3 configs have been tried.
Fold-to-fold SD is about 0.07, and fold 3 is weak for every config (0.57-0.63), so differences of 0.01-0.02 between configs are within noise. Run 1 vs run 3 is a mean gap of 0.02.

PR-AUC of about 0.73 with ROC-AUC of about 0.94 is strong for a label of undocumented origin. The PotentialFraud label may be a rule-based or investigator-flagged proxy, so the model may be recovering the labelling rule rather than real fraud. Provider-level features such as volume or size may leak label information.

Run 1 uses the 'all' feature set, which includes size features. Size-based features may dominate the ranking and mostly surface large providers rather than suspicious ones. The no_size runs score lower but are not decisively worse.

Run 3 has the best precision@50 (0.784 vs 0.764), which is closer to the roughly 100-provider audit queue. It loses on the primary metric and on fold wins, but the precision@k gap could matter operationally.
Claims cover only about 13 months. It is unclear whether CV folds are temporal or random, so performance may be optimistic compared with forward-looking use.
Run 1 uses no imbalance handling. That is fine for PR-AUC but leaves open whether class_weight would help with the same feature set.

next_experiments.rationale: Apply run 3's more regularised params to the 'all' feature set with no imbalance handling. This isolates whether the feature set or the params explain run 1's edge, and tests whether a smoother model improves the weak folds.

A simple baseline checks whether the signal is mostly linear or label-rule-like. If it comes close to LightGBM, the simpler model is preferable under the tie-break rule, and it also helps flag possible leakage.

concerns: Run 4 wins 4 of 5 folds (1, 3, 4, 5). Only fold 2 goes to run 1, by a hair (0.7304 vs 0.7295). Run 4 beats run 1 by 0.0085 mean PR-AUC, a small margin relative to the fold sd of about 0.066.

Fold-to-fold variation is large (fold 3 about 0.64 vs fold 4 about 0.81) and tracks across all configs. This suggests the folds differ in difficulty, or that the small positive count (about 500 flagged providers) makes PR-AUC noisy.

The PotentialFraud label has no documented origin, so it is suspicion rather than confirmed fraud. High PR-AUC (about 0.74) and ROC-AUC (about 0.946) may reflect the model learning the labelling process, or leakage from provider size or volume features, rather than true fraud.

Run 3, which drops size features and adds agent features, scores only about 0.03 lower than run 4. Run 2 (no_size random forest) is lower still. This suggests size features add modest signal and that much of the signal is not size-driven. Even so, ROC-AUC above 0.94 deserves scrutiny.

Claims cover only about 13 months, and the fold split is not described. If folds are not grouped or time-aware, there may be optimistic leakage. Precision@50 of about 0.79 is the more relevant operational number for a queue of about 100, and precision at 100 was not reported.
Class weighting did not help in run 3, and run 4 without imbalance handling is best. The calibration of the score for ranking has not been examined, but ranking is all the audit queue needs.
Only 4 configs were tried. Run 4 is a simpler, more regularized variant of run 1 and wins, which suggests that further tuning is likely to give only marginal gains within the noise.

review.split_comment: Stratified provider-level 5-fold CV keeps each provider in a single fold and preserves the 9.35% flagged rate, which is suitable for PR-AUC. Features are per-provider aggregates, so there is no cross-fold leakage apart from the unclear scope of dup_any_provider. A time-based check would be a useful supplement, since claims span only about one year, and the undocumented label origin means results measure agreement with suspicion flags rather than confirmed fraud.

1.rationale: Strong gradient boosting baseline on all features with no resampling, since PR-AUC ranking depends on calibrated ordering and the 9.35% positive rate is moderate. Small leaves and a large min_child_samples limit overfitting on 5,410 providers.

2.rationale: Removing size features (claim volume proxies) tests whether the ranking relies on provider size rather than behavioral signal, which matters for audit fairness and for avoiding a queue filled with large providers. Random forest with class weights offers a robust, low-variance comparison.

3.rationale: A lower-capacity boosted model without size features but with agent features, using class weighting, tests whether behavioral and agent signals alone yield a competitive top-100 ranking with less size dependence.

4.rationale: Apply run 3's more regularised params to the 'all' feature set with no imbalance handling. This isolates whether the feature set or the params explain run 1's edge, and tests whether a smoother model improves the weak folds.
